source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Malingering by definition, because any memory gap after trauma indicates intentional symptom production","B":"Normal forgetfulness because trauma cannot be associated with clinically important memory disruption","C":"A dissociative disorder involving disruption of memory that warrants further mental-health evaluation","D":"Antisocial personality disorder because autobiographical amnesia is a defining diagnostic feature"}}
source_row.rationale: Dissociative disorders can involve disruption of memory and may be associated with trauma. A diagnosis requires clinical evaluation and exclusion of neurologic, substance-related, and other causes; the presentation should not be labeled malingering without evidence.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical features: inability to recall important autobiographical information, often associated with trauma or stress, beyond ordinary forgetting; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: After trauma, a client has significant gaps in memory for important autobiographical information that exceed ordinary forgetfulness. Which condition should be considered?
